title: Active suspension research · 01
label: CONTROL THEORY · RESEARCH LOG
description: A quarter-car model, a nominal backstepping baseline, and two reinforcement-learning designs.
body:
I am studying reinforcement learning for adaptive control of a quarter-car active suspension. The first milestone is a checked plant model and a nominal backstepping baseline.

Two designs on the same plant

The first design uses actor–critic learning for the virtual and actual inputs in backstepping. The second investigates simplified reinforcement learning on the same plant. Body displacement has relative degree two in a four-state model, so the second design must account for wheel dynamics and check the conditions for a high-order fully actuated form.

First simulation

With a healthy actuator and a 5 Hz road input of 0.02 m amplitude, body acceleration RMS over 20 seconds fell from 1.966 with zero commanded force to 0.564 m/s² with nominal backstepping. Dynamic tire force RMS rose from 1393 to 1420 N. At the 0.02 cm amplitude also stated in the source, acceleration RMS rose from 0.357 to 0.564 m/s². These figures include the initial transient. The intended road amplitude remains open.

The simulation checks force balance and the actuator fault transitions. The next milestone is to establish the costs, states and stability conditions for both designs before implementing the learning controllers.

Suspension model and parameters · Simplified reinforcement learning

title: A quieter bot is a better bot
label: SOFTWARE · FIELD NOTE 01
description: On-demand weather and bounded background work.
body:
Useful automation should leave a little room for everyone else. A group-chat bot is no exception.

Fetch when there is a reason

A weather binding is a preference, not a reason to query every provider forever. The bot fetches a region when someone asks, when a greeting needs it, or when an explicitly configured notification is due. A short per-region cache serves nearby requests; a per-region lock prevents simultaneous requests from repeating the same work.

Keep slow work off the conversation path

Research, video metadata and image recognition can take longer than an ordinary message. Independent jobs, concurrency bounds and time budgets let those tasks finish without making unrelated groups wait. A model listing alone does not prove a model can answer: successful ordinary responses build a preference queue instead.

Collect less, preserve better

A picture is not necessarily a sticker. Explicit sticker metadata and actual GIF headers are stronger evidence than a word in a CDN URL. Oversized non-GIF candidates can be quarantined with their original bytes and index backed up.

These are notes about the project, not a claim that every provider or network failure has been eliminated.

title: What survives in a hardware archive?
label: HARDWARE · FIELD NOTE 02
description: Recovering technical sources without overstating a prototype's capabilities.
body:
An old project folder is a record of a process, not automatically a working product. Recovery starts with that distinction.

Keep the parts that can be understood

The fire-rescue vehicle archive retains an ESP32-CAM camera subsystem, infrared remote notes and reviewed CAD drawings. It is not a complete, validated autonomous vehicle. Navigation, chassis and pump behavior cannot be inferred from a camera sketch.

Separate configuration from source

Network credentials belong in a private configuration header. A public example shows the required names without real Wi-Fi information. CAD author metadata and unrelated documents are not necessary to understand the technical export.

Test the claim you can actually test

Offline checks validate archive structure, protocol constants and source relationships. They do not establish that a board package compiles or that hardware behaves safely. Those need build and bench-testing stages. The recovered recording setup sits inside a successful Wi-Fi branch; documenting that limitation is better than repeating an old claim about offline recording.

Explore the recovered subsystem ↗

title: A public map, with private boundaries
label: SOFTWARE · FIELD NOTE 03
description: Shareable recommendations without private bot records.
body:
A public recommendation invites someone to explore a place, not inspect another person's private records.

Start with an explicit public feed

The atlas imports venue names, cities, public addresses, coordinates, categories and original article links from the published public food-map JSON. Reviews, ratings, photographs, companions and personal comments are not copied. Each place links back to its original source.

Make the boundary structural

This website has a separate repository and deployment. It does not read weather bindings, QQ identifiers, profiles, private maps, chats or stickers. The public updater uses one fixed HTTPS feed once daily, not on every page visit.

Coordinates have a context

The source uses GCJ-02. Amap links retain those coordinates. The optional OpenStreetMap view uses an approximate WGS84 conversion: a discovery aid, not a surveying or navigation instrument. For precision, check the venue in its original map service.

The site never requests your location. The venue list works without interactive tiles.

title: Spleeter Local
label: LOCAL AUDIO
description: Split local audio and video into vocals and accompaniment.
body:
The original Windows package bundled a localized Spleeter runner, TensorFlow and the 2-stem model. The repository documents where each dependency comes from and provides a Python command-line wrapper.

FFmpeg checks the first audio stream before inference. Spleeter then writes two stereo WAV files. Audio files and videos with sound can be processed on the machine.

title: Magic Eraser
label: LOCAL IMAGE REPAIR
description: Repair a masked area locally with the Big LaMa model.
body:
A white mask marks the area to rebuild from its surroundings. Black pixels stay unchanged. The Python tool runs on the CPU and saves the result as a new PNG.

The local checkpoint matches the fingerprint recorded by IOPaint. The repository includes setup instructions and links to the upstream model. Results depend on how much of the scene the mask covers.

title: A small site, with clear boundaries
label: PRIVACY & SOURCES
description: What this website publishes and where its data comes from.
body:
An independent notebook without advertising analytics or private bot records.

Public content and sources

Project notes and venue facts are public. Original names and recommendation links are preserved. Check sources before travelling; acknowledgements are collected on About.

Private records stay separate

The site never reads bot contacts, profiles, weather bindings, chats, screenshots or sticker databases, and does not connect to a home computer.

Browser and maps

Theme and language preferences may be saved in your browser. A first-party frostmoon_theme cookie stores only light or dark for up to one year so the server can match the first paint to your choice; it is not an identifier or analytics cookie. No geolocation is requested. Maps load only on request; Amap or OpenStreetMap then receive normal network information such as IP addresses. The list works without map tiles.

Owner editing

The studio uses a server-verified password and a secure HTTPOnly session cookie valid for one hour. There are no visitor accounts. Drafts remain in browser memory unless exported. Saving sends a selected public document to GitHub, followed by a separate build and deployment. Never add secrets or private records to public content. Credentials stay in server runtime secrets.

Corrections

Hosting services and GitHub may process operational logs under their own policies. For corrections or removal, open a repository issue without sensitive information.

Friend applications and resources

Submitting a friend-link application stores public website metadata and review state in a private Cloudflare D1 database, outside GitHub. Pending and rejected entries are not public. Only owner-approved website details are displayed. The form does not request an email, QQ account, medical record or password. A request-IP hash is used for rate limiting, not saved in the application table. External resource sites have their own privacy policies and regional service limits. Request correction or withdrawal through the existing public contact channels without sending sensitive information.
